title: Sharing a new skill with a glance-at-me
summary: Most children show what they can do, saying glance at me, by about 30 months, the milestone sheet says.
body: The words in sheet's example are glance at me, used to pull a caregiver into a feat. The milestone is sharing the feat, not a required sentence. A point or a tug that does the same job is not graded here. The series defines most as 75 percent or more, says the materials are not a validated screen, and gives a US age.

sources.title: Milestones by 30 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US government public domain. Supports 'Shows you what she can do by saying, Look at me!'.
